$comment: Machine-readable record of the reclaim policy for this Mac.  Neither
scripts/hoghunter-clean nor Sources/Storage/DiskCleaner.swift reads it at
run time, so the code decides and this states it; a test requires every
engine rule to be listed here with a tier its code really gives.  Every
tier assignment is a lesson from the BF-HOUSEKEEPER wake log -- do not
relax a tier without a measured reason.

replaces.cleanmymac: Uninstalled 2026-09-30. A stale `brew list` entry survives (cleanmymac-cli) with no Cellar dir and `command -v` returns 1, so every cleanmymac call was a silent no-op. All callers now use hoghunter-clean.

tiers.$comment: What each tier means to scripts/hoghunter-clean, and when the run may touch it.
tiers.safe: Every run, including the watch's cheap band.
tiers.semi-safe: Only --band=full, which the pressure triggers take on any hit: 25 GB free or less, a 15 GB drop in free space at any level, swap, or load.  A rule with maxFreeGb also needs the disk at or under that line, enforced per rule in the code and read again from df before each delete.
tiers.expensive: Only --band=full while the disk is acute or critical (under 40 GB free).  Bulk deletes that are the biggest wins and the biggest I/O bursts.

bands.$comment: OWNER RULING 2026-10-02 (Jay): pressure changes the SHAPE of the work (2-4 bounded chunks), never its SCOPE. The previous rule -- 'swap >= 90 OR load1 > 40 => do less' -- was a guard whose threshold sat INSIDE this host's normal operating band: load1 runs 15-30 here continuously from real fleet build work, so it was true almost always, and wedded to a near-permanent swap reading it meant cleaning almost never ran. A guard whose threshold equals the normal state is an outage, not a guard. Deleting caches never reduces swap, and that still holds -- but it constrains what fixes swap, NOT how much regenerable waste may be cleared.

chunking.$note: A chunk is 2-3 targets with a df + uptime re-read between. Verified 2026-10-02 21:24: 3 chunks, ~1.9G by du, load1 25.7 -> 15.1, zero process kills.

cheapOnlyWhen.$deprecated: Retained for reporting and as the EXPENSIVE-tier context only. These must never suppress the safe or semi-safe tiers. The load1 threshold in particular is true nearly always on this host and so cannot gate work.

thrashDetection.$why: load1 counts uninterruptible page-in as running, so it is a LAGGING indicator. High load1 with HIGH cpu idle and kernel_task absent from the top-CPU sample is real work, not thrash (2026-10-02 21:00: load1 25.68, 27% idle).

idlenessGates.$comment: No file touched in N minutes proves nothing is mid-write.

rules.name: snapshots
rules.title: APFS / Time Machine local snapshots
rules.$rationale: The single largest reclaim on a Mac that backs up to an external destination. A local snapshot pins Data-volume container space; the backup itself is on the destination disk, so deleting a local snapshot does NOT touch the backup. macOS recreates one on the next backup. This is a shrink, not a loss.
rules.whySemiSafe: Held back under CHEAP-ONLY. Also surfaced to Jay: the count of snapshots on this Mac is itself a signal that the backup cadence is faster than the disk can absorb.

rules.name: temp-scratch
rules.title: Orphaned per-user temp scratch
rules.$rationale: Long-lived fleet artifacts in DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR. `ssr` nests sit under RANDOM-named parents, so a top-level glob misses them -- enumerate with find -maxdepth 3 -type d -name ssr and filter on the leaf's mtime. `.com.openai.codex.*` are FILES, not directories: find -type d returns 0 and du -sh on each is wasted work. Classes are KB-scale at thousands of entries (botfleet-dsh-mcp-*, omb-*, mmx-scope-*, bf-ui-shim-*) and are deliberately not scanned.

rules.name: app-staging
rules.title: Extracted but unused app updaters
rules.$rationale: Sparkle/electron-updater leave an extracted .app plus the source zip. Gated on the OWNING updater process, not on lsof: an active ShipIt can report zero open handles while actively writing. `ShipIt` on this Mac belongs to Grok Bot (com.anysphere.sand.ShipIt) more often than to Claude, so the product name is matched from the path, never the generic name.
neverWhile: a process matching the product name is alive

rules.name: dev-caches
rules.title: Package manager and toolchain caches
rules.$rationale: All rebuild on next use. node-gyp, electron, electron-builder, deno, copilot, swiftpm, ms-playwright, npm _cacache, uv, pip, yarn. pnpm and gradle are only touched when the build fan-out is quiet -- on this Mac the fan-out is what drives load and swap, and disturbing it makes things worse.

rules.name: app-caches
rules.title: Per-application cache directories
rules.$rationale: The measured hog on this Mac was ~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm at 3.6 GB, with Codex (624 MB), pnpm (552 MB), antigravity (349 MB) and electron (248 MB) on top of it. The old rule set named a handful of specific toolchain caches and nothing else, so a host whose space went into app caches got nothing back. Everything under ~/Library/Caches is rebuildable by its app. In Application Support and the container trees only the cache-shaped children are touched (Cache, CachedData, Code Cache, GPUCache, logs, CacheStorage) -- everything else there is app state and stays untouched.
skipWhenAny: a file under the path was touched in the last 90 minutes
any process holds the path open

rules.name: agent-state
rules.title: Transient state left behind by coding agents
rules.$rationale: The agents are the fleet's own workers and they write logs, scratch files and caches beside their state. Those rebuild; the sessions and transcripts beside them do not. So the transient parts (logs, tmp, .tmp, cache, debug, shell-snapshots) are deleted and the session history (sessions, projects, history, conversations) is reported ask-first instead of deleted.  ~/.codex/.tmp holds marketplace clones that Codex's config names as live sources, so a tree holding any .git stays.
skipWhenAny: a file under the path was touched in the last 90 minutes
any process holds the path open

rules.name: xcode-artifacts
rules.title: Xcode DerivedData and device support
rules.$rationale: Per-project DerivedData with no build running. iOS DeviceSupport for OS versions older than 7 days is in the expensive tier: it re-downloads when an old device is attached. A lone xcodebuild with zero compiler children hours old is STALLED, not a real build -- check for clang/swiftc children before assuming work is in flight.

rules.name: simulator-runtimes
rules.title: iOS simulator runtimes
rules.$rationale: Historically the biggest single win on this Mac (18.55 GB measured 2026-09-27). Fully re-downloadable from Xcode. Deleting a runtime does NOT touch CoreSimulator/Devices, which stays ask-first. Verified after the 09-27 pass: 3 devices and 2.3 GB of user simulator state intact.
rules.$tierNote: This file said semi-safe until 2026-11-04 while the code filed these under expensive.  The code is what runs and nothing reads this field, so the words were corrected rather than widening the delete to the semi-safe band.

rules.name: duplicate-sim-runtimes
rules.title: Duplicate simulator runtime images
rules.$rationale: Disk images live in Apple's secure storage under /System/Library/AssetsV2, which simulator-runtimes never looks at.  Measured 2026-11-04: two iOS 27.2 images of 7.75 GB each, one never used.  Only when two or more Ready images share a runtime identifier and version.  A victim is a Disk Image with lastUsedAt null or older than the most recently used one, reports deletable true, and is never the image `simctl runtime match list` chooses, so at least one per version always stays.  That chooser speaks for one Xcode, so with any other number of Xcodes there is no candidate.  Output that does not read true gives no candidate, and that includes an absent lastUsedAt.  It calls simctl only when CoreSimulatorService is already alive, because simulator-runtimes stays shut while the service runs and simctl starts it.  Asked again right before the delete.
skipWhenAny: more or fewer than one Xcode installed
simctl output is unparseable or unrecognised
the chooser's build is not among the Ready images

rules.name: tool-versions
rules.title: Superseded versions of installed tools
rules.$rationale: Versioned stores whose layout has been read: muse-bin-* in ~/.local/bin (with its .muse-version pointer), ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions and ~/.local/share/claude/versions.  Keeps the newest two by mtime, what the default launcher resolves to, and any version a symlink, wrapper or LaunchAgent names.  With no proof of what the default launcher runs, or a store holding more than versions, the tool is left out.  ~/.local/share/claude/stable is not versioned and is not touched.
skipWhenAny: any process holds it open (a running binary shows in the listing)
its access time is under 7 days old
the tool holds a lock on it

rules.name: xcode-scratch
rules.title: Xcode-shaped build scratch in /private/tmp
rules.$rationale: What xcodebuild -derivedDataPath leaves behind (3.69 GB measured 2026-11-04).  Direct children only, owned by this user, holding Build with Xcode's output folders and an Xcode cache beside it.  HH-180 is why the name and age of a temp folder prove nothing: the top level is an allowlist, every entry below it is judged against what Xcode writes there, a walk that cannot finish refuses, the identity is bound at scan time, and every gate is asked again on a fresh open-file listing right before the delete.  A writer that starts after that is the limit HH-180 records.
skipWhenAny: a nested repository other than a provable SwiftPM clone

rules.name: stale-build-output
rules.title: Stale ignored build output in main checkouts
rules.$rationale: Owner's request of 2026-11-04 ('teach HH wherever possible') narrows the playbook's manual-only stance for these four names, and only at 25 GB free or less.  .build, .next, build and target directly in ~/Code/<repo>, or a path named per repo, spelled exactly so on disk.  git must ignore it and track nothing in it, and it must be unchanged for 14 days.  A tree that misses a check stays on the ask-first report with the reason.  node_modules and dist stay report-only.
skipWhenAny: any process has its working directory in the repo
a nested repository other than a provable SwiftPM clone
it holds keys, archives, notes, project files, another kind of repository, or source at its top level

rules.name: botfleet-rollback
rules.title: Abandoned BotFleet update/rollback copies
rules.$rationale: An update moves the running tree aside and installs a fresh copy.  The rollback rebuilds with a reinstall; the first day is a grace period for a manual rollback.  Listed here on 2026-11-04, where it was missing.

rules.name: logs
rules.title: Unbounded logs (tail-truncated)
rules.$rationale: The shrink operation CleanMyMac gets wrong. Deleting a log file while a daemon holds the fd leaves the daemon writing to an unlinked inode, so the space is NOT freed until that daemon restarts. Truncating IN PLACE fixes it. Keeps the last 16 MB -- the tail is what an operator reads.

rules.name: sqlite-wal
rules.title: Oversized SQLite WAL (checkpointed)
rules.$rationale: A large -wal beside a live database is double storage. A checkpoint TRUNCATE folds it into the main file and zeroes the WAL in constant time. Unlike VACUUM it does not rewrite the database, so it is safe on a 14 GB file. Measured on Coolify app.db 2026-09-30: freelist_count=1 means VACUUM would reclaim ~4 KB while rewriting 14.7 GB -- the WAL is the correct lever, the VACUUM is not.
refusesWhen: another process holds the database open

rules.name: brew
rules.title: Homebrew obsolete versions
rules.$rationale: brew cleanup --prune=all keeps the current version and symlinks. Skipped while any brew or node-gyp process is alive. 67 MB typical, so it is never worth acting on alone.

rules.name: ask-first
rules.title: Ask-first inventory (report only, never auto-applied)
rules.$rationale: Surfaced so Jay or the Housekeeper can act with explicit OK instead of re-deriving the inventory. Nothing in this tier is ever deleted by the engine.
items: Google DriveFS local cache (content cache + Logs only under Application Support/Google/DriveFS; Resources are program files -- KEEP)
Claude / Monet / Parall vm_bundles (claudevm.bundle, ~10 GB; only when pgrep -x Claude = 0 AND lsof bundle = 0)
~/apps/botfleet-* trees (may hold a seat's uncommitted work)
idle build output the stale-build-output rule cannot take, with the reason, and every idle node_modules and dist
Documents, photos, secrets, any path under ~/Library/CloudStorage

hardRules.neverRmRf: rm -rf is intercepted by the mavis-trash layer on this Mac: it reports success, removes the inodes, and moves the bytes to ~/.Trash, freeing NOTHING. Every delete goes through `find <dir> -depth -delete`, and reclaim is verified with a fresh df -- never the exit code.
hardRules.neverPs: Never bare `ps`, `pgrep -l`, `pgrep -fl`, or `ps -o comm` -- argv on this Mac carries live API keys and lands them in logs. Count with `pgrep -f X | wc -l` or `pgrep -x`.
hardRules.neverLsofPlusD: lsof +D HANGS past 60s on big trees. Ask about the exact path, or corroborate with mtime.
hardRules.neverOptimizeRam: Purging resident pages into swapfiles converts RAM pressure into disk usage on the same APFS container -- the opposite of the goal. Measured +3.6 to +7.3 GB swap per run.
hardRules.neverEmptyTrash: mavis-trash parks deleted files in ~/.Trash. Never empty it without asking.
hardRules.neverAppleDeleting: $TMPDIR/Deleting-<UUID> with thousands of files fresh is ACTIVE Apple staging (stuck update, APFS snapshot, bsdtar extraction). Do not touch. Only an empty data/ subtree with no live children AND mtime > 7d is an orphan.
hardRules.noTimeoutCommand: macOS has no `timeout` (exit 127). Use run_in_background + job_output, or a Python subprocess timeout.
